docs.title: Spinfinity
docs.text:
Python package for simulating quantum spin systems in tunnel junction experiments.

Available at: GitHub - WillkeLab/Spinfinity

docs.title: Intended Use
docs.text:
Spinfinity is intended for researchers working on quantum spin systems in scanning probe microscopy. The package is designed for modeling spin structures in double-barrier tunnel junctions, solving their spin Hamiltonians, and simulating observables that can be compared to experimental spectroscopy data.

Typical use cases include:

  • modeling single-spin and multi-spin systems
  • calculating eigenenergies and eigenstates of custom spin Hamiltonians
  • simulating tunneling-induced transition rates and steady-state populations
  • computing differential conductance spectra for comparison with experiment
  • computing Electron Spin Resonance spectra and related driven dynamics
  • simulating the time evolution of spin systems in the tunneling junction
  • simulating pulsed ESR experiments such as Rabi oscillations

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Read the User guide for the code structure and typical workflows. Follow the tutorials for worked examples.

docs.title: Plot display settings
docs.text:
Set the default once per Python session or notebook:

from spinfinity import plotting

plotting.set_display_mode("responsive")

Use "fixed" for each plot's preferred width, "responsive" to fill the available width, or "no" to suppress display. These settings apply to all package plotting functions. Override a single call with show="fixed", show="responsive", or show="no"; the default show=None inherits the setting.

docs.title: Helperfunctions
docs.text:
The helperfunctions module provides a Fourier transform calculation and three fitting functions:

Function Model Parameter order fit_fano Symmetric Lorentzian peak or dip with constant offset [A, x0, FWHM, C] fit_exponential Exponential decay with constant offset [A, T, C] fit_oscillation Exponentially damped cosine with constant offset [A, T, f, phi, C]

The fitting functions return xfit, yfit, popt, and perr: a dense plotting grid, the fitted curve, the fitted parameters, and their estimated one-standard-deviation uncertainties.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Spinfinity requires Python 3.11 or newer. Its numerical and plotting dependencies are installed automatically.

We recommend using a separate Python environment for Spinfinity.

docs.title: Download the project
docs.text:
Clone the repository:

git clone https://github.com/WillkeLab/Spinfinity.git
cd Spinfinity

Alternatively, download the repository using Code → Download ZIP on GitHub, extract it, and open a terminal in the extracted folder.

If you already have a local checkout, use that folder instead.

Run the remaining installation commands from the project root—the folder containing pyproject.toml.

docs.title: Create an environment
docs.text: Choose either a virtual environment or a Conda environment. You do not need both.

docs.title: Virtual environment
docs.text:
On Windows, using PowerShell:

py -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

If your Python installation uses python instead of py, use python -m venv .venv to create the environment.

On Linux or macOS:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

Activate this environment whenever you open a new terminal to work with Spinfinity.

docs.title: Conda environment
docs.text:
If you already use Conda, you can create a dedicated environment instead:

conda create -n spinfinity python=3.12 pip
conda activate spinfinity

Run these commands in a terminal where Conda is available, such as Anaconda Prompt or Miniconda Prompt.

docs.title: Install Spinfinity
docs.text:
With your environment activated, run:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip
python -m pip install -e .

The -e option installs Spinfinity in editable mode: changes to the local Python source are used without reinstalling the package. Restart an already-running notebook kernel after changing imported code.

If you change dependencies in pyproject.toml, run the installation command again.

For a non-editable installation, use python -m pip install . instead.

docs.title: Verify the installation
docs.text:
Check that Spinfinity can be imported and inspect its location:

python -c "import spinfinity; print(spinfinity.__file__)"

For an editable installation, the printed path should point to your local checkout.

Then run this example in Python or a notebook:

from spinfinity import SpinSys, hamil

spin = SpinSys([0.5])
spin.B = [0.0, 0.0, 0.5]  # T
spin.BTip = [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]  # T
spin.gfactorvector = [2.0]

hamil.calc_EigEnergies(spin, rebuildH=True)

print("Relative eigenenergies (meV):", spin.E_All)

The two relative energies should be approximately [0.0, 0.05788382] meV.

Continue with the first spin Hamiltonian tutorial.

docs.title: Run notebooks
docs.text:
For notebooks in VS Code, install Python kernel support in the same environment:

python -m pip install ipykernel

Install the VS Code Python and Jupyter extensions. Open a notebook and use Select Kernel to choose your Spinfinity environment.

If you prefer JupyterLab:

python -m pip install jupyterlab
python -m jupyterlab

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
This step is optional. From the project root, install the documentation dependencies and Python kernel support:

python -m pip install -e ".[docs]" ipykernel

Start the local documentation server:

python -m mkdocs serve

Open the address printed in the terminal, normally http://127.0.0.1:8000. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

To generate the static website without starting a server:

python -m mkdocs build

The website is generated in site/. Tutorial notebooks are executed during the build, so building takes longer than rendering Markdown alone.

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text:
Spinfinity uses ordinary numerical values and NumPy arrays. Units are not attached to these objects and are not converted automatically. Inputs must therefore use the units specified below.

This page describes the active Python implementation. Conventions from other programs, including the Scilab code, should not be assumed to match without checking operator definitions and prefactors.

docs.title: Parameter units
docs.text:
Attribute or argument Unit Meaning Spins Dimensionless Spin quantum numbers, for example 0.5, 1, or 2.5. ReadoutSpin Dimensionless index Zero-based index of the spin used for readout and RF excitation. gfactorvector Dimensionless Signed g-factors used with the Bohr magneton. B, BTip T Cartesian magnetic-field vectors in the order [x, y, z]. T K Bath temperature. See the zero-temperature note below. Dvector, EvectorX, EvectorY meV Coefficients of the quadratic anisotropy terms. Jvector meV Diagonal pair-exchange coefficients [Jxx, Jyy, Jzz]. Jxy, Jxz, Jyz, Jyx, Jzx, Jzy meV Off-diagonal pair-exchange coefficients. Avector meV Diagonal pairwise hyperfine coefficients [Axx, Ayy, Azz]. Qvector meV Quadrupolar Hamiltonian coefficients [Qxx, Qyy, Qzz], not physical quadrupole moments. Stevens meV Coefficients multiplying the package's dimensionless Stevens operators. DipoleVector meV Dipolar coupling strengths D0, one value per spin pair. AtomPositions Dimensionless Cartesian lattice coordinates, not positions directly in nm. latticeLengthXY nm Three componentwise lattice spacings [ax, ay, az], despite the historical attribute name. V_DC, V_array mV Bias voltage and voltage-sweep values. G_st A/V = S Conductance scale used to normalize tip–sample scattering. G_ss A/V = S Conductance-equivalent substrate-scattering parameters, one per spin. G_tt Dimensionless Switch: 0 disables and 1 enables tip–tip scattering. It is not a conductance. U Dimensionless Potential-scattering amplitude relative to the spin-exchange scattering amplitude. b0 Dimensionless Fraction assigned to the spin-independent background channel. TipPolarization, SamplePolarization Dimensionless Cartesian polarization vectors. Zero denotes an unpolarized reservoir; vector norm one denotes full polarization. J Dimensionless Signed substrate exchange per spin in the legacy spin-code normalization; negative denotes antiferromagnetic exchange. Not Jvector. J_tip Dimensionless Signed virtual tip exchange attribute of Spinsysused in third-order functions; default zero. Independent phenomenological parameter, not inferred from G_tt. w, lt meV Electronic bandwidth and positive lifetime broadening used in third-order spectroscopy. energy_step meV Internal integration spacing for third-order calculations; verify convergence by reducing it. B1 T Peak amplitude of the linearly oscillating RF magnetic field in the ESR-rate model. T2 ns Total transverse coherence time used in the ESR-rate model. T_phi ns Phenomenological local pure-dephasing time, not total T2. Positive infinity disables this contribution. freq, freq_array, f_RF GHz Ordinary frequency, not angular frequency. RabiRate GHz Ordinary Rabi frequency used in coherent-control routines. The ESR-rate routines instead use B1. lw GHz Lorentzian full width at half maximum in ESR.calc_FreqSweep. time_array, pulsewidth_array, tau ns Evolution times, pulse durations, and delays in Lindblad and coherent-control routines.

All Zeeman terms use the Bohr magneton. The code does not automatically distinguish electronic and nuclear spins. When modeling a nucleus using a nuclear g-factor defined with the nuclear magneton, use the equivalent coefficient:

g_effective = g_nuclear * mu_N / mu_B

docs.title: Calculated quantities
docs.text: Quantity Unit Convention H meV Hamiltonian in the product-spin basis. E_sort meV Sorted eigenenergies before subtracting the ground-state energy. E_All meV Sorted eigenenergies relative to the ground state. E_All_inGHz GHz Relative eigenenergies divided by Planck's constant. eigVectors Dimensionless Normalized eigenvectors stored as columns. Sx, Sy, Sz Dimensionless Spin operators with the factor of hbar removed. Populations, pop_0 Dimensionless Eigenstate occupation probabilities. Density matrices Dimensionless Trace-one matrices. calc_RateIntegrals(...) meV Electron phase-space integrals, not transition rates. MatrixST, MatrixTS, MatrixSS, MatrixTT Dimensionless Squared scattering amplitudes before conductance and phase-space prefactors. Rates, Rates_Summed, ESRRates 1/s Population-transition or scattering-event rates. K 1/s Classical population-rate generator. T_state_tot, T_state_ss s Inverse total or substrate-only inelastic escape rates of individual eigenstates. elastic_dephasing_rates 1/s Pairwise coherence-decay rates, not population-transfer rates. collapse_ops, elastic_collapse_ops 1/sqrt(ns) Collapse operators prepared for evolution with time in ns. H_RF rad/ns Rotating-frame generator used by the time-evolution solver. Tunnel currents, I_off A Signed currents. Unnormalized rate-based ESR signal A Current difference I_RF_on - I_RF_off. Unnormalized second-order dI/dV A/V = S Differential conductance. Mag, Mag_tot Dimensionless Spin expectation values, not magnetic moments in SI units. Fourier frequencies GHz When the supplied sampling times are in ns.

docs.title: Ordinary frequency versus angular frequency
docs.text:
Public frequency inputs are ordinary frequencies:

omega [rad/ns] = 2*pi * f [GHz]

For time evolution, the Hamiltonian is converted from energy into an angular-frequency generator:

H_generator = H * meVtoGHzConversion * 2 * np.pi

Do not apply this conversion twice. In particular, H_RF is already in rad/ns.

Bath rates are converted separately:

rate [1/ns] = rate [1/s] * 1e-9

Consequently, an inelastic collapse operator is constructed as:

L_ij = sqrt(rate_ij [1/s] * 1e-9) * |j><i|

Rates are multiplied by 1e-9; collapse amplitudes are multiplied by its square root.

docs.title: Spin operators
docs.text:
The matrices represent dimensionless angular momentum:

Sz |m> = m |m>
[Sx, Sy] = i Sz

For spin one-half:

Sx = sigma_x / 2
Sy = sigma_y / 2
Sz = sigma_z / 2

Do not insert an additional factor of hbar into Hamiltonian terms that already use the package constants and coefficients.

docs.title: Zeeman term convention
docs.text:
The external-field contribution is:

H_Z = -sum_i g_i * muB * B.S_i

docs.title: User guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how Spinfinity is organized, which modules to use, and how to move from model parameters to calculated results.

Start with Installation if the package is not installed. Use this page as a map, then follow the tutorials for complete worked examples. The API documentation provides function signatures, parameters, return values and implementation details.

docs.title: The central object: SpinSys
docs.text:
A SpinSys object holds the physical inputs and the results needed by the calculation modules. Most workflows reuse the same object, conventionally named spin.

For example, SpinSys([0.5]) represents one spin-1/2; SpinSys([1.0, 0.5]) represents a spin-1 site coupled to a spin-1/2 site. Spin indices start at zero. The Hilbert-space dimension is the product of 2*S + 1 over all sites.

Typical inputs include:

  • B and BTip: external and tip magnetic fields.
  • gfactorvector, Dvector and interaction parameters: the spin Hamiltonian.
  • T, V_DC, conductances and reservoir polarizations: the electron bath.
  • ReadoutSpin: the site addressed by the tip and coherent drive.

Calculation functions subsequently attach results such as H, E_All, eigVectors, Rates and Populations. These quantities are not all calculated when the object is created.

See the SpinSys reference for the available attributes.

docs.title: Modules and use cases
docs.text: Module What to use it for SpinSys Define the spin sites and store model inputs and calculated results. SpinHamiltonian (hamil) Construct spin operators and Hamiltonians; calculate energies and eigenstates. Includes Zeeman fields, anisotropy, exchange, dipolar, hyperfine, quadrupolar and Stevens terms. Bath (bath) Calculate electron-scattering rates, thermal or pumped populations, tunnel current and eigenstate escape lifetimes. dIdV Calculate and plot IETS spectra. Choose thermal second order ("2nd") or a rate-equation treatment ("2ndR"); the plotting interface also dispatches third-order modes. dIdV3 Add perturbative third-order corrections, using thermal populations ("3rd") or corrected stationary rate equations ("3rdR"). This is a weak-coupling treatment, not a strong-coupling Kondo solver. ESR Calculate continuous-wave ESR spectra and tip-field maps. Choose phenomenological lines or a driven steady-state rate model. SpinPumping Explore voltage-dependent populations, rates and magnetization; project coupled-system populations onto subsystem states. Lindblad (lind) Construct inelastic and phenomenological dephasing collapse operators; simulate dissipative time evolution and analyze its observables. CoherentControl (CC) Simulate driven pulse experiments using rotating-frame descriptions: Rabi, Ramsey, Hahn echo and ESEEM. Eigensystem_Import Parse energies, state compositions and Stevens coefficients from supported CASSCF/RASSI output. This is a separate parser, not an automatic replacement of a SpinSys eigensystem. helperfunctions Fit symmetric spectral peaks or dips, exponential decays and damped oscillations. plotting Set global or per-call display modes for the package's Plotly figures.

docs.title: How calculations fit together
docs.text:
The usual starting point is a solved Hamiltonian. Subsequent steps depend on the observable of interest; not every calculation requires every branch.

flowchart TD
    SYS(["`**SpinSys**<br/>Physical inputs`"])
    HAM["`**SpinHamiltonian**<br/>Hamiltonian, eigenenergies and eigenstates`"]

    SYS --> HAM
    HAM --> SPECTRA["`**dIdV** & **ESR**<br/>Thermal IETS and phenomenological ESR`"]
    HAM --> BATH["`**Bath**<br/>Rates and stationary populations`"]

    BATH --> CURRENT["`**dIdV** & **dIdV3**<br/>Higher order IETS`"]
    BATH --> ESR["`**ESR**<br/>Rate-based ESR`"]
    BATH --> SP["`**SpinPumping**<br/>Voltage dependent state populations and magnetization`"]
    BATH --> LIND["`**Lindblad**<br/>Collapse operators and time evolution`"]
    LIND --> CC["`**CoherentControl**<br/>Pulsed ESR and coherent control`"]

Typical calculation workflow. The arrows indicate how calculated quantities feed subsequent analyses, not an exhaustive internal function-call graph.

docs.title: Quick example: a spin-1/2 ESR spectrum
docs.text:
The following example defines a single spin, solves its Hamiltonian and calculates a phenomenological ESR spectrum. A small tilted tip field gives nonzero transition and detection weights.

import numpy as np

from spinfinity import ESR, SpinSys, bath, hamil

spin = SpinSys([0.5])
spin.B = [0.0, 0.0, 0.5]  # T
spin.BTip = [0.01, 0.0, 0.01]  # T
spin.gfactorvector = [2.0]
spin.T = 0.5  # K

hamil.calc_EigStates(spin, rebuildH=True)
bath.calc_Populations(spin, AllowPumping=False)

resonance = spin.E_All_inGHz[1] - spin.E_All_inGHz[0]
frequencies = np.linspace(resonance - 0.2, resonance + 0.2, 1001)
frequencies, signal = ESR.calc_FreqSweep(
    spin,
    freq_array=frequencies,
    lw=0.02,  # GHz; FWHM
    norm=False,
    output=False,
)

print("Relative energies (meV):", spin.E_All)
print(f"Transition frequency: {resonance:.6f} GHz")
print("Spectrum shape:", signal.shape)

E_All contains energies relative to the ground state; the columns of eigVectors are the corresponding eigenvectors in the product-spin basis.

The first Hamiltonian tutorial explains the eigensystem. The ESR tutorial adds the physical interpretation and a plotted spectrum.

docs.title: Continue with the tutorials
docs.text:
The tutorials are practical, sequential examples rather than a second API reference. For a first visit, begin with the Hamiltonian tutorial, then choose the observable or experiment you want to simulate.

Tutorial What it adds to this guide First spin Hamiltonian Solve and inspect a single-spin eigensystem; change parameters and rebuild. Two interacting spins Assign pair exchange and interpret coupled eigenstates. IETS Compare thermal second-order conductance with tunneling-induced pumping. Phenomenological ESR Generate and interpret a Lorentzian ESR spectrum. Relaxation and time evolution Configure dissipation and simulate relaxation from an initial state. Rabi oscillations Configure a resonant drive and calculate driven population dynamics.

For more specialized systems, explore the repository's examples/ notebooks. Use the API documentation when you need exact arguments, return structures or the assumptions of an individual function.

docs.title: Bath
docs.text:
Calculations and visualizations related to the electron bath coupled to the spin system.

This module provides functions to calculates various physical quantities based on the second order tunneling theory. It most importantly calculates the tunneling rates and matrix elements. From this various physical quantities can be derived, such as magnetization, lifetimes, tunneling current, and population distributions.

Functions:

Name Description calc_Magnetization

Calculate the magnetization of the given SpinSys object along a specified axis.

calc_Lifetimes

Calculate the escape lifetimes for each state of the given SpinSys object.

calc_TunnelCurrent

Calculate the tunneling current of the given SpinSys object.

calc_Populations

Calculate the population distribution of spin states of the given SpinSys object.

calc_Rates

Calculate transition rates of the given SpinSys object and tunnel parameters.

calc_RateIntegrals

Calculate rate integrals of the given SpinSys object and scattering parameters.

calc_TunnelingMatrixElements

Calculate the tunneling matrix elements for the SpinSys and scattering type.

calc_TunnelingElectronMatrixElements

Calculate tunneling electron matrix elements of the given SpinSys object.

plot_Populations

Plot the thermal and steady state populations of the given SpinSys object.

plot_RateContributions

Plot the contributions of the highest N transition rates between spin states.

plot_RatesTo

Plot the rate contributions to a specified state of the given SpinSys object.

plot_RatesFrom

Plot the rate contributions from a specified state of the given SpinSys object.

Dependencies
  • Uses spinfinity.SpinSys.SpinSys class to represent the spin system and its properties.
  • Uses spinfinity.SpinHamiltonian for eigenvalue and eigenvector calculations.
References
  • Ternes, M., Spin excitations and correlations in scanning tunneling spectroscopy. New J. Phys. 17, 063016 (2015). https://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/17/6/063016
  • Loth, S., von Bergmann, K., Ternes, M. et al. Controlling the state of quantum spins with electric currents. Nature Phys 6, 340–344 (2010). https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys1616

docs.title: calc_Lifetimes(spinsys)
docs.text:
Calculate the escape lifetimes for each state of the given SpinSys object.

This function computes the total and natural lifetimes for each state in the given spin system by summing the transition rates out of each state. If the rate matrix is not already calculated, it will be computed.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spinsys SpinSys

The spin system object containing state information and rate matrices.

required Notes

The function updates the following attributes of spinsys:

  • spinsys..T_state_tot: The total lifetime for each state, considering all possible transitions.
  • spinsys..T_state_ss: The natural lifetime for each state, considering only sample-sample scattering.
Source code in spinfinity\Bath.py 
def calc_Lifetimes(spinsys: SpinSys):
    """
    Calculate the escape lifetimes for each state of the given `SpinSys` object.

    This function computes the total and natural lifetimes for each
    state in the given spin system by summing the transition rates out
    of each state. If the rate matrix is not already calculated, it
    will be computed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing state information and rate matrices.

    Notes
    -----
    The function updates the following attributes of `spinsys`:

    - `spinsys..T_state_tot`: The total lifetime for each state, considering
    all possible transitions.
    - `spinsys..T_state_ss`: The natural lifetime for each state,
    considering only sample-sample scattering.
    """
    # Check whether the RateMatrix is already calculated
    if not hasattr(spinsys, "Rates") or spinsys.Rates is None:
        calc_Rates(spinsys)

    # Initialize the Rate array that somes up all rates that leave the state
    R1_tot = np.zeros(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)
    R1_ss = np.zeros(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)

    # Summing up all rates that leave the state
    for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):  # i is the initial state
        for j in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):  # j is the final state
            if i != j:
                R1_tot[i] += spinsys.Rates_Summed[i, j]  # Summing up all the rates
                R1_ss[i] += spinsys.Rates[2, i, j]  # Just sample sample scattering

    spinsys.T_state_tot = 1 / R1_tot  # Total state escape lifetime
    spinsys.T_state_ss = 1 / R1_ss  # natural state escape lifetime from s-s scattering

    return

docs.title: calc_Magnetization(spinsys, type='z', AllowPumping=True)
docs.text:
Calculate the magnetization of the given SpinSys object along a specified axis.

This function calculates the magnetization of a spin system by projecting the spin operators onto the eigenstates of the system and weighting them by the population of each state. The magnetization can be calculated along the 'x', 'y', or 'z' axis.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spinsys SpinSys

The spin system object containing eigenvectors, spin operators, and populations.

required type str

The axis along which to calculate magnetization ('x', 'y', or 'z'). Default is 'z'.

'z' AllowPumping bool

Whether to allow population pumping during calculation. Default is True.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description Mag ndarray

A 1D array containing the magnetization for each individual spin.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If type is not one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.

Notes

The function updates the following attributes of spinsys:

- Mag_tot: The total magnetization of the system.
- Mag_tot_max: The maximum possible total magnetization.
- Mag: The magnetization for each individual spin.
- Mag_max: The maximum possible magnetization for each spin.
- Magtype: The axis along which magnetization was calculated.
Source code in spinfinity\Bath.py 
def calc_Magnetization(spinsys: SpinSys, type: str = "z", AllowPumping: bool = True):
    """
    Calculate the magnetization of the given `SpinSys` object along a specified axis.

    This function calculates the magnetization of a spin system by projecting the spin
    operators onto the eigenstates of the system and weighting them by the population of
    each state. The magnetization can be calculated along the 'x', 'y', or 'z' axis.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing eigenvectors, spin operators, and populations.
    type : str, optional
        The axis along which to calculate magnetization ('x', 'y', or
        'z'). Default is 'z'.
    AllowPumping : bool, optional
        Whether to allow population pumping during calculation. Default is True.

    Returns
    -------
    Mag : np.ndarray
        A 1D array containing the magnetization for each individual spin.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `type` is not one of 'x', 'y', or 'z'.

    Notes
    -----
    The function updates the following attributes of `spinsys`:

        - Mag_tot: The total magnetization of the system.
        - Mag_tot_max: The maximum possible total magnetization.
        - Mag: The magnetization for each individual spin.
        - Mag_max: The maximum possible magnetization for each spin.
        - Magtype: The axis along which magnetization was calculated.
    """
    if not hasattr(spinsys, "Populations") or spinsys.Populations is None:
        calc_Populations(spinsys, AllowPumping=True)

    Populations = spinsys.Populations if AllowPumping else spinsys.pop_0

    # Choose the Operator based on the type of magnetization
    if type == "x":
        S = spinsys.Sx
    elif type == "y":
        S = spinsys.Sy
    elif type == "z":
        S = spinsys.Sz
    else:
        raise ValueError("Invalid type for magnetization. Choose 'x', 'y', or 'z'.")

    S_Operator = np.sum(S, axis=0)

    # Initialize the magnetization arrays
    # Individual projection
    S_elements = np.zeros((spinsys.NSpins, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))
    # Projection of the total spin system
    S_elements_tot = np.zeros(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)
    Mag = np.zeros(spinsys.NSpins)
    Mag_tot = 0

    # Itterate through every eigenstate and each spin
    for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
        S_elements_tot[i] = np.real(
            spinsys.eigVectors[:, i].T.conj() @ S_Operator @ spinsys.eigVectors[:, i]
        )
        Mag_tot += S_elements_tot[i] * Populations[i]
        for j in range(spinsys.NSpins):
            S_elements[j, i] = np.real(
                spinsys.eigVectors[:, i].T.conj()
                @ S[j, :, :]
                @ spinsys.eigVectors[:, i]
            )
            Mag[j] += S_elements[j, i] * Populations[i]

    # Remember the maximum value for each spin to have the opportunity to normalize
    Mag_tot_max = S_elements_tot.max()
    Mag_max = S_elements.max(axis=1)

    # Store the magnetization in the spinsys object
    spinsys.Mag_tot = Mag_tot  # Store the total magnetization in the spinsys object
    spinsys.Mag_tot_max = Mag_tot_max  # Store the maximum magnetization
    spinsys.Mag = Mag  # Store the individual magnetizations in the spinsys object
    spinsys.Mag_max = Mag_max  # Store the maximum magnetization for each spin in
    spinsys.Magtype = type  # Store the type of magnetization calculated

    return Mag

docs.title: calc_Populations(spinsys, AllowPumping=True)
docs.text:
Calculate the population distribution of spin states of the given SpinSys object.

Computes the thermal population distribution based on Boltzmann statistics. If pumping is allowed, calculates the non-thermal population by solving the steady-state of the rate equations.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spinsys SpinSys

def calc_Populations(spinsys: SpinSys, AllowPumping: bool = True):
    """
    Calculate the population distribution of spin states of the given `SpinSys` object.

    Computes the thermal population distribution based on Boltzmann statistics.
    If pumping is allowed, calculates the non-thermal population by solving the
    steady-state of the rate equations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing energy levels, temperature,
        and other relevant parameters.
    AllowPumping : bool, optional
        If True, calculates the non-thermal population considering pumping.
        Default is True.

    Notes
    -----
    If pumping is not allowed or no valid solution is found for the non-thermal
    population, the thermal population is used.
    The function updates the following attributes of `spinsys`:

    - `spinsys.pop_0`: The normalized thermal population distribution.
    - `spinsys.Populations`: The final population distribution considering pumping
        if allowed, otherwise the thermal population.
    - `spinsys.K`: The rate matrix used for solving the steady-state population.
    """
    if not hasattr(spinsys, "E_All") or spinsys.E_All is None:
        hamil.build_Hamiltonian(spinsys)
        hamil.calc_EigEnergies(spinsys)

    # Calculate the thermal population in any case
    spinsys.pop_0 = calc_ThermalPopulations(spinsys)

    # If pumping is allowed, calculate the non-thermal population
    if AllowPumping:
        # Calculate the rates if not already done
        if not hasattr(spinsys, "Rates") or spinsys.Rates is None:
            calc_Rates(spinsys)
        spinsys.K = np.zeros((spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))

        for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
            for j in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
                if i != j:
                    # Rates leaving state i
                    spinsys.K[i, i] -= spinsys.Rates_Summed[i, j]
                    # Rates leading to state i
                    spinsys.K[i, j] = spinsys.Rates_Summed[j, i]
        # Solve the Rate equation to get the steady-state populations
        if AllowPumping:
            try:
                p = null_space(spinsys.K)
            except Exception as e:
                print("Warning: null_space failed, using thermal population. Error:", e)
                p = np.empty((0, 0))
        if p.size == 0:  # If no valid solution, use thermal distribution
            spinsys.Populations = spinsys.pop_0
        else:
            spinsys.Populations = p[:, 0] / np.sum(p[:, 0])
    else:
        spinsys.Populations = spinsys.pop_0

    return

def calc_RateIntegrals(spinsys: SpinSys, type: str):
    """
    Calculate rate integrals of the given `SpinSys` object and scattering parameters.

    The function calculates the rate integrals for tip-to-sample (ts), sample-to-tip
    (st), sample-to-sample (ss), and tip-to-tip (tt) scattering processes based on the
    energy levels of the spin system, the bias voltage, and the temperature.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        An instance of the SpinSys class containing system parameters
        such as energy levels, Boltzmann constant, temperature, and
        matrix dimension.
    type : str
        The type of transition to calculate. Must be one of:
        - 'ts': tip to sample
        - 'st': sample to tip
        - 'ss': sample to sample
        - 'tt': tip to tip

    Returns
    -------
    RateIntegrals : np.ndarray
        A 2D numpy array of shape (dimensionOfMatrix, dimensionOfMatrix) containing the
        calculated rate integrals for each pair of energy levels.
    """
    # Create the three nxn matrices [I_ts, I_st, I_ss]
    RateIntegrals = np.zeros((spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))

    V_DC = spinsys.V_DC

    thermal_energy = spinsys.kB * spinsys.T

    for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
        for j in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
            delta_E = spinsys.E_All[j] - spinsys.E_All[i]
            if type == "ts":
                transition_energy = delta_E - V_DC
            elif type == "st":
                transition_energy = delta_E + V_DC
            elif type == "ss" or type == "tt":
                transition_energy = delta_E
            else:
                continue

            if thermal_energy == 0:
                # Zero-temperature limit
                RateIntegrals[i, j] = max(-transition_energy, 0.0)
            else:
                x = transition_energy / thermal_energy

                # If the argument is very small, use a Taylor expansion to avoid
                # numerical issues
                if abs(x) < 1e-8:
                    # Expansion of x / (exp(x) - 1)
                    RateIntegrals[i, j] = thermal_energy * (1.0 - x / 2.0 + x**2 / 12.0)
                elif x > 50:
                    # Algebraically equivalent form that avoids exp(x) overflow
                    exp_minus_x = np.exp(-x)
                    RateIntegrals[i, j] = (
                        thermal_energy * x * exp_minus_x / (1.0 - exp_minus_x)
                    )
                else:
                    RateIntegrals[i, j] = thermal_energy * x / np.expm1(x)

    return RateIntegrals

  • spinsys.Rates_Summed: A 2D array containing the sum of all transition rates for each state pair.

def calc_Rates(spinsys: SpinSys):
    """
    Calculate transition rates of the given `SpinSys` object and tunnel parameters.

    The function calculates the transition rates for tip-to-sample (ts), sample-to-tip
    (st),sample-to-sample (ss), and tip-to-tip (tt) scattering processes based on the
    tunneling matrix elements and rate integrals. It uses the tunnel parameters defined
    in the `spinsys` object.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing all relevant parameters and matrices.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If tip-tip scattering is enabled and G_ss[ReadoutSpin] is not positive.

    Notes
    -----
    The function updates the following attributes of `spinsys`:

    - `spinsys.Rates`: A 3D array containing the calculated transition rates for each
        scattering process and state pair.
    - `spinsys.Rates_Summed`: A 2D array containing the sum of all transition rates
        for each state pair.
    - `spinsys.MatrixST`: The tunneling matrix elements for sample-tip scattering.
    - `spinsys.MatrixTS`: The tunneling matrix elements for tip-sample scattering.
    - `spinsys.MatrixSS`: The tunneling matrix elements for sample-sample scattering.
    - `spinsys.MatrixTT`: The tunneling matrix elements for tip-tip scattering.
    """
    # Initialize the Rates matrix
    spinsys.Rates = np.zeros((4, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))

    # Calculate the Eignevalues and Eignevectors if not already done
    if not hasattr(spinsys, "eigVectors") or spinsys.eigVectors is None:
        hamil.build_Hamiltonian(spinsys)
        hamil.calc_EigEnergies(spinsys)

    # Getting the relevant matrix elements
    spinsys.MatrixST = calc_TunnelingMatrixElements(spinsys, "st")[0]
    spinsys.MatrixTS = spinsys.MatrixST.T
    spinsys.MatrixSS = calc_TunnelingMatrixElements(spinsys, "ss")
    spinsys.MatrixTT = calc_TunnelingMatrixElements(spinsys, "tt")[0]

    MatrixSS_summed = np.zeros((spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))

    for i in range(spinsys.NSpins):
        MatrixSS_summed += spinsys.MatrixSS[i, :, :] * spinsys.G_ss[i]

    # Calculating the 3 different integrals
    RateIntegrals_ts = calc_RateIntegrals(spinsys, "ts")
    RateIntegrals_st = calc_RateIntegrals(spinsys, "st")
    RateIntegrals_ss = calc_RateIntegrals(spinsys, "ss")
    # RateIntegrals_tt = spinsys.calc_RateIntegrals(spinsys.V_DC, 'tt')

    Rate_0 = spinsys.MatrixST[0][0]  # Transition matrix element of the ground state

    # Rate-Factors using Loth et al. (2010), https://doi.org/10.1038/nphys1616
    # G_st_prime is the effective tunneling conductance
    G_st_prime = (1 - spinsys.b0) * spinsys.G_st

    RateFactor_ts = G_st_prime / (const.e * Rate_0) / 1e3
    RateFactor_st = G_st_prime / (const.e * Rate_0) / 1e3
    # The G_ss value might differ for each spin, so it was incorporated
    # earlier when summing the matrix.
    RateFactor_ss = 1 / (const.e * Rate_0) / 1e3
    RateFactor_tt = 0.0
    if spinsys.G_tt:
        if spinsys.G_ss[spinsys.ReadoutSpin] <= 0:
            raise ValueError("G_tt requires positive G_ss for the readout spin.")
        RateFactor_tt = (
            G_st_prime**2
            / spinsys.G_ss[spinsys.ReadoutSpin]
            / (const.e * Rate_0)
            / 1e3
            * spinsys.G_tt
        )

    # Calculate rates based on rate factors and integrals
    spinsys.Rates[0, :, :] = RateFactor_ts * spinsys.MatrixTS * RateIntegrals_ts
    spinsys.Rates[1, :, :] = RateFactor_st * spinsys.MatrixST * RateIntegrals_st
    spinsys.Rates[2, :, :] = RateFactor_ss * MatrixSS_summed * RateIntegrals_ss
    spinsys.Rates[3, :, :] = RateFactor_tt * spinsys.MatrixTT * RateIntegrals_ss

    # Sum the rates
    spinsys.Rates_Summed = (
        spinsys.Rates[0, :, :]
        + spinsys.Rates[1, :, :]
        + spinsys.Rates[2, :, :]
        + spinsys.Rates[3, :, :]
    )

    return

def calc_ThermalPopulations(spinsys: SpinSys):
    """
    Calculate equilibrium populations in the energy eigenbasis.

    E_All must already be calculated and contain energies in meV.
    T is in K. At T=0, exactly degenerate ground states are equally occupied.
    This function does not modify spinsys.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing energy levels, temperature,
        and other relevant parameters.

    Returns
    -------
    np.ndarray
        The normalized thermal population distribution of the spin states.
    """
    energies = np.asarray(spinsys.E_All, dtype=float)
    energies = energies - np.min(energies)

    if spinsys.T == 0:
        weights = (energies == 0).astype(float)
    else:
        weights = np.exp(-energies / (spinsys.kB * spinsys.T))

    return weights / np.sum(weights)

def calc_TunnelCurrent(spinsys: SpinSys, AllowPumping: bool = True):
    """
    Calculate the tunneling current of the given `SpinSys` object.

    The tunneling current is calculated using the populations of the spin states. If
    the populations are not already calculated, they will be computed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing energy levels, populations,
        rates, and other relevant parameters.
    AllowPumping : bool, optional
        If True, allows for non-thermal population effects (default is True).

    Returns
    -------
    Current : float
        The calculated tunneling current.
    """
    # Rates are needed for both thermal and pumped current.
    if not hasattr(spinsys, "Rates") or spinsys.Rates is None:
        calc_Rates(spinsys)

    if AllowPumping:
        if not hasattr(spinsys, "Populations") or spinsys.Populations is None:
            calc_Populations(spinsys, AllowPumping=True)

        populations = spinsys.Populations
    else:
        spinsys.pop_0 = calc_ThermalPopulations(spinsys)
        populations = spinsys.pop_0

    # Deriving the tunneling current using Equation 41 from Ternes (2015),
    # https://dx.doi.org/10.1088/1367-2630/17/6/063016
    Current = 0
    for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
        for j in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
            Current_temp = (
                const.e
                * populations[i]
                * (spinsys.Rates[0, i, j] - spinsys.Rates[1, i, j])
            )
            Current += Current_temp

    # Adjust current calculation by adding the elastic contribution
    Current += spinsys.b0 * spinsys.G_st * spinsys.V_DC * 1e-3

    return Current

def calc_TunnelingElectronMatrixElements(spinsys: SpinSys, scattertype: str):
    """
    Calculate tunneling electron matrix elements of the given `SpinSys` object.

    This function computes the matrix elements associated with
    tunneling electrons between tip and sample, considering their spin
    polarizations. It normalizes the tip and sample polarizations if
    necessary, constructs the corresponding density matrices, and
    calculates the matrix elements for the specified scattering type
    ('st', 'tt', or 'ss').

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        An object representing the spin system, containing tip and sample polarizations.
    scattertype : str
        The type of scattering to calculate matrix elements for. Options are:
        - 'st': tip-to-sample scattering
        - 'tt': tip-to-tip scattering
        - 'ss': sample-to-sample scattering

    Returns
    -------
    x : ndarray
        Matrix elements for the x-component of spin.
    y : ndarray
        Matrix elements for the y-component of spin.
    z : ndarray
        Matrix elements for the z-component of spin.
    u : ndarray
        Matrix elements for the identity component.
    """
    # Normalize the Tip and Sample Polarizations if their norms are greater than 1
    if np.linalg.norm(spinsys.TipPolarization) > 1:
        spinsys.TipPolarization = spinsys.TipPolarization / np.linalg.norm(
            spinsys.TipPolarization
        )
    if np.linalg.norm(spinsys.SamplePolarization) > 1:
        spinsys.SamplePolarization = spinsys.SamplePolarization / np.linalg.norm(
            spinsys.SamplePolarization
        )

    # Get Spin-1/2 matrices (Pauli matrices) for electrons
    S_x, S_y, S_z = hamil.calc_AngMomMatrices(0.5)

    # Calculate the density matrices for tip and sample
    densityTip = (
        0.5 * np.eye(2)
        + spinsys.TipPolarization[0] * S_x
        + spinsys.TipPolarization[1] * S_y
        + spinsys.TipPolarization[2] * S_z
    )
    densitySample = (
        0.5 * np.eye(2)
        + spinsys.SamplePolarization[0] * S_x
        + spinsys.SamplePolarization[1] * S_y
        + spinsys.SamplePolarization[2] * S_z
    )

    # Calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the density matrices
    eigValTip_temp, eigVecTip = np.linalg.eig(densityTip)
    eigValSample_temp, eigVecSample = np.linalg.eig(densitySample)
    eigValTip = np.diag(eigValTip_temp)
    eigValSample = np.diag(eigValSample_temp)

    # Swap the eigen value order
    eigValTip[[0, 1], [0, 1]] = eigValTip[[1, 0], [1, 0]]
    eigVecTip[:, [0, 1]] = eigVecTip[:, [1, 0]]

    # Calculate the weights matrix as sqrt(diag(eigValSample) * diag(eigValTip))
    Weights_st = np.sqrt(np.outer(np.diag(eigValSample), np.diag(eigValTip)))
    Weights_tt = np.sqrt(np.outer(np.diag(eigValTip), np.diag(eigValTip)))
    Weights_ss = np.sqrt(np.outer(np.diag(eigValSample), np.diag(eigValSample)))

    x_st = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_x) @ eigVecTip),
        Weights_st,
    )
    y_st = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_y) @ eigVecTip),
        Weights_st,
    )
    z_st = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_z) @ eigVecTip),
        Weights_st,
    )
    u_st = np.multiply((2 * np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ eigVecTip), Weights_st)

    x_tt = np.multiply((np.conjugate(eigVecTip.T) @ (2 * S_x) @ eigVecTip), Weights_tt)
    y_tt = np.multiply((np.conjugate(eigVecTip.T) @ (2 * S_y) @ eigVecTip), Weights_tt)
    z_tt = np.multiply((np.conjugate(eigVecTip.T) @ (2 * S_z) @ eigVecTip), Weights_tt)
    u_tt = np.multiply((2 * np.conjugate(eigVecTip.T) @ eigVecTip), Weights_tt)

    x_ss = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_x) @ eigVecSample),
        Weights_ss,
    )
    y_ss = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_y) @ eigVecSample),
        Weights_ss,
    )
    z_ss = np.multiply(
        (np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ (2 * S_z) @ eigVecSample),
        Weights_ss,
    )
    u_ss = np.multiply((2 * np.conjugate(eigVecSample.T) @ eigVecSample), Weights_ss)

    matrix_elements = {
        "st": (x_st, y_st, z_st, u_st),
        "tt": (x_tt, y_tt, z_tt, u_tt),
        "ss": (x_ss, y_ss, z_ss, u_ss),
    }
    return matrix_elements.get(scattertype, (x_st, y_st, z_st, u_st))

def calc_TunnelingMatrixElements(spinsys: SpinSys, scattertype: str):
    """
    Calculate the tunneling matrix elements for the `SpinSys` and scattering type.

    This function computes the tunneling matrix elements for the specified scattering
    type ('st', 'ts', 'ss', or 'tt') by combining the electron tunneling matrix elements
    with the spin operators of the system. The resulting matrix elements are calculated
    in the eigenbasis of the spin system and are used to determine the transition rates
    for different scattering processes.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        An instance of the SpinSys class containing the spin system
        properties, eigenvectors, and spin operators (Sx, Sy, Sz, U).
    scattertype : str
        Type of scattering process. If "ss", calculations are performed for all spins;
        otherwise, calculations are performed for the readout spin only.

    Returns
    -------
    RateMatrix : np.ndarray
        Array containing the calculated tunneling rate matrix elements. The shape is
        (NSpins, dimensionOfMatrix, dimensionOfMatrix) for "ss" scattertype, and
        (1, dimensionOfMatrix, dimensionOfMatrix) otherwise.
    """
    # Get the electron tunneling matrix elements
    x_el, y_el, z_el, u_el = calc_TunnelingElectronMatrixElements(spinsys, scattertype)

    # Initialize RateMatrix
    if scattertype == "ss":
        RateMatrix = np.zeros(
            (spinsys.NSpins, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)
        )
        N = spinsys.NSpins
        Index = np.arange(N)
    else:
        RateMatrix = np.zeros((1, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix, spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix))
        N = 1
        Index = np.array([spinsys.ReadoutSpin])

    # x_el, y_el, z_el, and u_el are 2x2 matrices flattened to 4 elements.
    for k in range(N):
        MatrixX = (
            np.conjugate(np.transpose(spinsys.eigVectors))
            @ spinsys.Sx[Index[k], :, :]
            @ spinsys.eigVectors
        )
        MatrixY = (
            np.conjugate(np.transpose(spinsys.eigVectors))
            @ spinsys.Sy[Index[k], :, :]
            @ spinsys.eigVectors
        )
        MatrixZ = (
            np.conjugate(np.transpose(spinsys.eigVectors))
            @ spinsys.Sz[Index[k], :, :]
            @ spinsys.eigVectors
        )
        MatrixU = (
            spinsys.U[Index[k]]
            * np.conjugate(np.transpose(spinsys.eigVectors))
            @ spinsys.eigVectors
        )

        for i in range(2):
            for j in range(2):
                RateMatrix[k][:][:] += (
                    np.abs(
                        MatrixX * x_el[i][j]
                        + MatrixY * y_el[i][j]
                        + MatrixZ * z_el[i][j]
                        + MatrixU * u_el[i][j]
                    )
                    ** 2
                )

    return RateMatrix

def plot_RateContributions(
    spinsys: SpinSys,
    yscale: str = "linear",
    N=None,
    ylim: list = None,
    show: str | None = None,
):
    """
    Plot the contributions of the highest N transition rates between spin states.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        The spin system object containing the states, rates, and matrix dimension.
    yscale : str, optional
        The scale for the y-axis ('linear' or 'log'). Default is 'linear'.
    N : int, optional
        The number of highest rate transitions to display. If None, all
        transitions are shown (default is None).
    ylim : list of float, optional
        The limits for the y-axis as [ymin, ymax]. If None, no limits
        are set (default is None).

    show : {"fixed", "responsive", "no"} or None, optional
        Display mode. ``None`` uses the global setting, initially ``"fixed"``.
        ``"fixed"`` uses the preferred width; ``"responsive"`` fills the
        container width. ``"no"`` suppresses display without skipping calculations.

    Returns
    -------
    return_dict : dict
        A dictionary containing:
        - 'fig': plotly.graph_objects.Figure
            The plotly figure object containing the plot.
    """
    hamil.calc_EigStates(spinsys)
    calc_Rates(spinsys)

    labels = ["ts", "st", "ss", "tt"]
    colors = ["blue", "orange", "green", "red"]

    # Build a list of all transitions (i -> f) for i != f
    all_transitions = [
        (i, f)
        for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)
        for f in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix)
        if i != f
    ]
    transition_labels_all = [
        f"{spinsys.statesWithoutE[i]} → {spinsys.statesWithoutE[f]}"
        for (i, f) in all_transitions
    ]

    def safe_rate(r):
        return (
            0.0 if (r is None or (isinstance(r, float) and np.isnan(r))) else float(r)
        )

    if N is None:
        # Prepare y-values for each rate contribution type across all transitions
        data = []
        for idx in range(4):
            y_vals = [safe_rate(spinsys.Rates[idx][i, f]) for (i, f) in all_transitions]
            data.append(
                go.Bar(
                    name=labels[idx],
                    x=transition_labels_all,
                    y=y_vals,
                    marker_color=colors[idx],
                    opacity=0.7,
                    hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + labels[idx] + ": %{y}<extra></extra>",
                )
            )

        fig = go.Figure(data=data)
        fig.update_layout(
            barmode="stack",
            title="Rate Contributions",
            xaxis=dict(title="Transitions", tickangle=45),
            yaxis=dict(
                title="Rate",
                type="linear" if yscale == "linear" else yscale,
                autorange=True,
            ),
            plot_bgcolor="white",
            paper_bgcolor="white",
            legend=dict(
                orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1
            ),
        )
        fig.update_yaxes(exponentformat="e", showexponent="all")
        if ylim is not None:
            fig.update_yaxes(range=ylim)
        plotting.show_figure(fig, preferred_width=1200, show=show)

    else:
        # Collect all transitions and their total rates, ignoring NaNs
        transitions = []
        for i in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
            for f in range(spinsys.dimensionOfMatrix):
                if i != f:
                    total_rate = sum([spinsys.Rates[idx][i, f] for idx in range(4)])
                    if not (isinstance(total_rate, float) and np.isnan(total_rate)):
                        transitions.append(((i, f), total_rate))

        # Sort by total_rate descending and keep top N
        transitions = sorted(transitions, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:N]
        if len(transitions) == 0:
            fig = go.Figure()
            fig.update_layout(
                title=f"Top {N} Rate Contributions (no valid transitions)",
                plot_bgcolor="white",
                paper_bgcolor="white",
            )
            fig.update_yaxes(exponentformat="e", showexponent="all")
            plotting.show_figure(fig, preferred_width=1200, show=show)
            return

        selected_pairs = [t[0] for t in transitions]
        transition_labels = [
            f"{spinsys.statesWithoutE[i]} → {spinsys.statesWithoutE[f]}"
            for (i, f) in selected_pairs
        ]

        data = []
        for idx in range(4):
            y_vals = [safe_rate(spinsys.Rates[idx][i, f]) for (i, f) in selected_pairs]
            data.append(
                go.Bar(
                    name=labels[idx],
                    x=transition_labels,
                    y=y_vals,
                    marker_color=colors[idx],
                    opacity=0.7,
                    hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + labels[idx] + ": %{y}<extra></extra>",
                )
            )

        fig = go.Figure(data=data)
        fig.update_layout(
            barmode="stack",
            title=f"Top {N} Rate Contributions",
            xaxis=dict(title="Transitions", tickangle=45),
            yaxis=dict(
                title="Rate",
                type="linear" if yscale == "linear" else yscale,
                autorange=True,
            ),
            plot_bgcolor="white",
            paper_bgcolor="white",
            legend=dict(
                orientation="h", yanchor="bottom", y=1.02, xanchor="right", x=1

        )
        fig.update_yaxes(exponentformat="e", showexponent="all")
        if ylim is not None:

def RotFrameSecular(spinsys, f_RF: float):
    """
    Rotating-frame Hamiltonian with the secular (RWA) approximation.

    Steps:
      a) quantization axis of the readout spin  n = B/|B|
         (add BTip here if it acts on the readout spin);
      b) Sz' = n . S_readout;  the frame rotates about n at f_RF;
      c) secular projection: keep only the part of H that commutes with the
         frame rotation, H_sec = sum_m P_m H P_m  (P_m projector on the
         Sz' eigenvalue m of the readout spin);
      d) H_RF = H_sec + 2*pi*f_RF*Sz'  (spinfinity Zeeman sign convention:
         H = -g*muB*B.S, so +f_RF*Sz' cancels the Zeeman term on resonance).

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        SpinSys object containing the spin system information.
    f_RF : float
        Frequency of the rotating frame in GHz.

    Returns
    -------
    H_RF : Qobj
        Rotating-frame Hamiltonian in angular GHz (rad/ns).

    Notes
    -----
    Also stores the tilted pulse/readout operators on spinsys:
    spinsys.Sz_rot, spinsys.Sx_rot, spinsys.Sy_rot
    Use Sx_rot as the pulse operator and Sy_rot/Sz_rot for detection.
    f_RF in GHz, H_RF returned in angular GHz (rad/ns), like RotFrame.
    """
    i = spinsys.ReadoutSpin

    # First handle the type of the tip
    if spinsys.tip == "a":
        Bvec = np.array(spinsys.B) - np.array(spinsys.BTip)
    else:
        Bvec = np.array(spinsys.B) + np.array(spinsys.BTip)

    n = Bvec / np.linalg.norm(Bvec)

    Sz_r = n[0] * spinsys.Sx[i] + n[1] * spinsys.Sy[i] + n[2] * spinsys.Sz[i]

    # transverse axes of the tilted frame (x' in the plane of lab-x and n)
    ref = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    if abs(np.dot(ref, n)) > 0.99:
        ref = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 0.0])
    x_p = ref - np.dot(ref, n) * n
    x_p /= np.linalg.norm(x_p)
    y_p = np.cross(n, x_p)
    Sx_r = x_p[0] * spinsys.Sx[i] + x_p[1] * spinsys.Sy[i] + x_p[2] * spinsys.Sz[i]
    Sy_r = y_p[0] * spinsys.Sx[i] + y_p[1] * spinsys.Sy[i] + y_p[2] * spinsys.Sz[i]

    # secular projection of the full static Hamiltonian
    H = spinsys.H * spinsys.meVtoGHzConversion * 2 * np.pi
    evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(Sz_r)
    H_sec = np.zeros_like(H)
    for m in np.unique(np.round(evals, 6)):
        V = evecs[:, np.abs(evals - m) < 1e-6]
        P = V @ V.conj().T
        H_sec = H_sec + P @ H @ P

    H_RF = H_sec + f_RF * Sz_r * 2 * np.pi

    spinsys.Sz_rot, spinsys.Sx_rot, spinsys.Sy_rot = Sz_r, Sx_r, Sy_r
    spinsys.H_RF = Qobj(H_RF)

    return spinsys.H_RF

def calc_3pulseESEEM_Parallel(
    spinsys: SpinSys,
    T_array: np.ndarray,
    tau: float,
    e_ops: list[Qobj] | None = None,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
):
    """
    Calculate a three-pulse ESEEM sequence in parallel.

    This function computes final expectation values after the sequence
    pi/2--tau--pi/2--T--pi/2--tau for each variable delay in ``T_array``. The
    calculation requires ``spinsys`` to contain ``f_RF``, ``RabiRate``, ``psi0``,
    and ``collapse_ops``, as well as a completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding
    spin operators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        SpinSys object containing the spin system information.
    T_array : np.ndarray
        Array of variable free-evolution times (in ns) between the second and third
        pi/2 pulses.
    tau : float
        Fixed free-evolution time (in ns) following the first and third pi/2 pulses.
    e_ops : list[Qobj], optional
        List of expectation operators to calculate. If None, defaults to the Sx,
        Sy, and Sz operators of the readout spin.
    n_jobs : int, optional
        Number of parallel worker processes used to evaluate the variable delays.
        ``-1`` uses all available CPU cores, while ``1`` runs serially.

    Returns
    -------
    T_array : np.ndarray
        Array of variable free-evolution times (in ns) used for the calculation.
    results : np.ndarray
        Two-dimensional array of final expectation values with shape
        ``(len(T_array), len(e_ops))``.

    Notes
    -----
    The fixed pi/2--tau--pi/2 prefix is calculated once. The remaining sequence is
    evaluated independently for each value in ``T_array`` using Joblib's ``loky``
    process backend.
    """
    T_array = np.asarray(T_array, dtype=float)

    if e_ops is None:
        readout_spin = spinsys.ReadoutSpin
        e_ops = [
            Qobj(spinsys.Sx[readout_spin]),
            Qobj(spinsys.Sy[readout_spin]),
            Qobj(spinsys.Sz[readout_spin]),
        ]
    else:
        e_ops = list(e_ops)

    # Constant free-evolution Hamiltonian.
    H_free = RotFrameSecular(spinsys, spinsys.f_RF)

    # Constant pulse Hamiltonian.
    Omega_R = 2.0 * np.pi * spinsys.RabiRate
    tp_90 = np.pi / (2.0 * Omega_R)

    pulse_op = Qobj(spinsys.Sx_rot)
    H_pulse = H_free + Omega_R * pulse_op

    psi0 = spinsys.psi0
    c_ops = spinsys.collapse_ops

    # Only retain the final state from each segment.
    options = {
        "store_states": False,
        "store_final_state": True,
        "progress_bar": "",
        "method": "diag",
    }

    def evolve_final(H, state, duration: float):
        duration = float(duration)

        if duration == 0.0:
            return state

        result = mesolve(
            H,
            state,
            [0.0, duration],
            c_ops=c_ops,
            e_ops=None,
            options=options,
        )

        return result.final_state

    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    # Fixed prefix:
    #
    #     pi/2 - tau - pi/2
    #
    # This is identical for every T and is therefore calculated once.
    # --------------------------------------------------------------
    state_after_prefix = evolve_final(
        H_pulse,
        psi0,
        tp_90,
    )

    state_after_prefix = evolve_final(
        H_free,
        state_after_prefix,
        tau,
    )

    state_after_prefix = evolve_final(
        H_pulse,
        state_after_prefix,
        tp_90,
    )

    def calc_point(T: float):
        state = state_after_prefix

        # Variable free-evolution interval.
        state = evolve_final(
            H_free,
            state,
            T,
        )

        # Third pi/2 pulse.
        state = evolve_final(
            H_pulse,
            state,
            tp_90,
        )

        # Fixed free-evolution interval.
        state = evolve_final(
            H_free,
            state,
            tau,
        )

        return np.asarray(expect(e_ops, state))

    if n_jobs == 1 or T_array.size <= 1:
        results = [calc_point(T) for T in T_array]
    else:
        results = Parallel(
            n_jobs=n_jobs,
            backend="loky",
            batch_size="auto",
        )(delayed(calc_point)(T) for T in T_array)

    return T_array, np.asarray(results)

This function evaluates the sequence pi/2--tau--pi/2--T--pi/2--tau--pi/2 using a four-step phase cycle on the first two pulses. The third and final pi/2 pulses retain the +x phase. The calculation requires spinsys to contain f_RF, RabiRate, psi0, and collapse_ops, as well as a completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding spin operators.

Parameters:

SpinSys object containing the spin system information.

required T_array ndarray

required tau float

Fixed free-evolution time (in ns) following the first and third pi/2 pulses.

required e_ops list[Qobj]

List of expectation operators to calculate. If None, defaults to the Sx, Sy, and Sz operators of the readout spin.

None n_jobs int

Notes

The four phase combinations are weighted as (+x, +x) - (-x, +x) - (+x, -x) + (-x, -x) and divided by four. Their fixed prefixes are calculated once, after which each value in T_array is evaluated independently using Joblib's loky process backend.

def calc_3pulseESEEM_pluspihalf_PhaseCycled(
    spinsys: SpinSys,
    T_array: np.ndarray,
    tau: float,
    e_ops: list | None = None,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
):
    """
    Calculate a phase-cycled three-pulse ESEEM sequence with a final pi/2 pulse.

    This function evaluates the sequence
    pi/2--tau--pi/2--T--pi/2--tau--pi/2 using a four-step phase cycle on the first
    two pulses. The third and final pi/2 pulses retain the +x phase. The calculation
    requires ``spinsys`` to contain ``f_RF``, ``RabiRate``, ``psi0``, and
    ``collapse_ops``, as well as a completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding spin
    operators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        SpinSys object containing the spin system information.
    T_array : np.ndarray
        Array of variable free-evolution times (in ns) between the second and third
        pi/2 pulses.
    tau : float
        Fixed free-evolution time (in ns) following the first and third pi/2 pulses.
    e_ops : list[Qobj], optional
        List of expectation operators to calculate. If
        None, defaults to the Sx, Sy, and Sz operators of the readout spin.
    n_jobs : int, optional
        Number of parallel worker processes used to evaluate the variable delays.
        ``-1`` uses all available CPU cores, while ``1`` runs serially.

    Returns
    -------
    T_array : np.ndarray
        Array of variable free-evolution times (in ns) used for the calculation.
    signal : np.ndarray
        Two-dimensional array of phase-cycled expectation values with shape
        ``(len(T_array), len(e_ops))``.

    Notes
    -----
    The four phase combinations are weighted as
    ``(+x, +x) - (-x, +x) - (+x, -x) + (-x, -x)`` and divided by four. Their fixed
    prefixes are calculated once, after which each value in ``T_array`` is
    evaluated independently using Joblib's ``loky`` process backend.
    """
    T_array = np.asarray(T_array, dtype=float)
    if e_ops is None:
        i = spinsys.ReadoutSpin
        e_ops = [Qobj(spinsys.Sx[i]), Qobj(spinsys.Sy[i]), Qobj(spinsys.Sz[i])]
    else:
        e_ops = list(e_ops)

    H_free = RotFrameSecular(spinsys, spinsys.f_RF)
    Omega_R = 2.0 * np.pi * spinsys.RabiRate
    tp_90 = np.pi / (2.0 * Omega_R)

    pulse_px = Qobj(spinsys.Sx_rot)  # +x pulse
    H_px = H_free + Omega_R * pulse_px
    H_mx = H_free - Omega_R * pulse_px  # -x pulse (180 deg phase)

    psi0 = spinsys.psi0
    c_ops = spinsys.collapse_ops
    options = {
        "store_states": False,
        "store_final_state": True,
        "progress_bar": "",
        "method": "diag",
    }

    def evolve_final(H, state, duration):
        if float(duration) == 0.0:
            return state
        res = mesolve(
            H, state, [0.0, float(duration)], c_ops=c_ops, e_ops=None, options=options
        )
        return res.final_state

    # four prefixes pi/2(ph1) - tau - pi/2(ph2), computed once each
    prefixes = {}
    for ph1, Hp1 in (("+x", H_px), ("-x", H_mx)):
        s = evolve_final(Hp1, psi0, tp_90)
        s = evolve_final(H_free, s, tau)
        for ph2, Hp2 in (("+x", H_px), ("-x", H_mx)):
            prefixes[(ph1, ph2)] = evolve_final(Hp2, s, tp_90)

    cycle = [
        (("+x", "+x"), +1.0),
        (("-x", "+x"), -1.0),
        (("+x", "-x"), -1.0),
        (("-x", "-x"), +1.0),
    ]

    def calc_point(T):
        acc = None
        for key, sign in cycle:
            s = evolve_final(H_free, prefixes[key], T)
            s = evolve_final(H_px, s, tp_90)  # 3rd pulse, fixed +x
            s = evolve_final(H_free, s, tau)
            s = evolve_final(H_px, s, tp_90)  # readout pi/2, fixed +x
            vals = np.asarray(expect(e_ops, s), dtype=float)
            acc = sign * vals if acc is None else acc + sign * vals
        return acc / 4.0

    if n_jobs == 1 or T_array.size <= 1:
        results = [calc_point(T) for T in T_array]
    else:
        results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, backend="loky", batch_size="auto")(
            delayed(calc_point)(T) for T in T_array
        )

    return T_array, np.asarray(results)

Calculate three-pulse ESEEM with an eight-step rephasing phase cycle.

The sequence is pi/2--tau--pi/2--T--pi/2--tau--pi/2. The first and final pulses have phase +x. The second and third pulse phases are cycled to select the rephasing stimulated-echo contribution.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default spinsys SpinSys

Spin system with a spin-one-half readout spin, a completed static Hamiltonian, and configured f_RF, RabiRate, psi0, and collapse_ops. The initial state may be a ket or a density matrix.

required T_array ndarray

One-dimensional array of finite, non-negative storage delays T in ns. The supplied ordering is preserved, and no zero is inserted.

required tau float

Finite, non-negative free-evolution delay in ns before the second pulse and after the third pulse.

required e_ops list[Qobj] or None

Observables measured after the final readout pulse. None uses Sz_rot of the readout spin, giving one signal column. Rephasing pathway selection assumes observables commuting with Sz_rot.

None n_jobs int

Number of parallel workers. The default -1 uses all available CPU cores; 1 evaluates the delays serially.

-1

Returns:

Name Type Description T_array ndarray

Storage delays T in ns, in the supplied order.

signal ndarray

Weighted mean of the eight expectation-value arrays, with shape (len(T_array), len(e_ops)), or (len(T_array), 1) for default readout. This is a signed quadrature signal, not a coherence magnitude.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If the readout spin is not one-half, T_array is not one-dimensional or contains negative or non-finite delays, tau is negative or non-finite, or RabiRate is non-positive or non-finite.

Notes

The cycle (phase_2, phase_3, weight), with phases in degrees, is (0, 0, +1), (180, 0, -1), (90, 90, -1), (270, 90, +1), (180, 180, +1), (0, 180, -1), (270, 270, -1), (90, 270, +1). Signals are divided by eight, without an additional amplitude rescaling.

For ideal pulses, electron-secular free evolution, and dissipation covariant under rotations about Sz_rot, this selects electron coherence orders p_1 = -p_3 = +/-1 and p_2 = 0. Finite pulses include the drift Hamiltonian and dissipation; pulse imperfections and nonsecular bath terms can leave residual unwanted contributions.

All Hamiltonians and collapse operators must be time-independent. Fixed pulse maps are reused, with one free-evolution map per storage delay. Liouville-space propagators are intended for small spin systems.

The nominal pi/2 duration is 1 / (4 * RabiRate) ns. Total sequence time is T + 2tau + 4t_pi2, but only T is returned.

Calls RotFrameSecular, updating H_RF, Sx_rot, Sy_rot, and Sz_rot on spinsys. The initial state, physical inputs, and collapse_ops are not changed. Rates and collapse operators must already be up to date.

    if spinsys.Spins[spinsys.ReadoutSpin] != 0.5:
        raise ValueError("The eight-step cycle requires a spin-one-half readout.")
    if T_array.ndim != 1 or not np.all(np.isfinite(T_array)) or np.any(T_array < 0):
        raise ValueError("T_array must contain finite, non-negative delays.")
    if not np.isfinite(tau) or tau < 0:
        raise ValueError("tau must be finite and non-negative.")
    if not np.isfinite(rabi_rate) or rabi_rate <= 0:
        raise ValueError("RabiRate must be finite and positive.")

    H_free = RotFrameSecular(spinsys, spinsys.f_RF)
    e_ops = [Qobj(spinsys.Sz_rot)] if e_ops is None else list(e_ops)

    if T_array.size == 0:
        return T_array, np.empty((0, len(e_ops)))

    Omega_R = 2.0 * np.pi * rabi_rate
    t_pi2 = np.pi / (2.0 * Omega_R)
    Sx = Qobj(spinsys.Sx_rot)
    Sy = Qobj(spinsys.Sy_rot)
    pulse_hamiltonians = {
        0: H_free + Omega_R * Sx,
        90: H_free + Omega_R * Sy,
        180: H_free - Omega_R * Sx,
        270: H_free - Omega_R * Sy,
    }

    # All maps act on vectorized density matrices, including unitary cases.
    L_free = liouvillian(H_free, spinsys.collapse_ops)
    free_tau = (L_free * tau).expm()
    pulse_maps = {
        phase: (liouvillian(H, spinsys.collapse_ops) * t_pi2).expm()
        for phase, H in pulse_hamiltonians.items()
    }

    rho0 = spinsys.psi0.proj() if spinsys.psi0.isket else spinsys.psi0
    state_after_tau = free_tau * pulse_maps[0] * operator_to_vector(rho0)
    prefixes = {
        phase: pulse_map * state_after_tau for phase, pulse_map in pulse_maps.items()
    }
    readout_maps = {
        phase: pulse_maps[0] * free_tau * pulse_map
        for phase, pulse_map in pulse_maps.items()
    }

    phase_cycle = [
        (0, 0, +1),
        (180, 0, -1),
        (90, 90, -1),
        (270, 90, +1),
        (180, 180, +1),
        (0, 180, -1),
        (270, 270, -1),
        (90, 270, +1),
    ]

    def calc_point(T):
        free_T = (L_free * float(T)).expm()
        stored_states = {phase: free_T * prefix for phase, prefix in prefixes.items()}

        signal = None
        for phase_2, phase_3, weight in phase_cycle:
            rho_final = vector_to_operator(
                readout_maps[phase_3] * stored_states[phase_2]
            )
            values = np.asarray(expect(e_ops, rho_final))
            signal = weight * values if signal is None else signal + weight * values

        return signal / 8.0

    if n_jobs == 1 or T_array.size <= 1:
        results = [calc_point(T) for T in T_array]
    else:
        results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs, backend="loky", batch_size="auto")(
            delayed(calc_point)(T) for T in T_array
        )

    return T_array, np.asarray(results)

def calc_HahnEcho_Parallel(
    spinsys: SpinSys,
    tau_array: np.ndarray,
    e_ops: list[Qobj] | None = None,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
):
    """
    Calculate a Hahn-echo sequence in parallel for multiple delay times.

    This function computes the final expectation values after a
    pi/2--tau--pi--tau pulse sequence. The calculation requires ``spinsys`` to
    contain ``f_RF``, ``RabiRate``, ``psi0``, and ``collapse_ops``, as well as a
    completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding spin operators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        SpinSys object containing the spin system information.
    tau_array : np.ndarray
        Array of non-negative free-evolution times (in ns) on either side of the pi
        pulse.
    e_ops : list[Qobj], optional
        List of expectation operators to calculate. If None, defaults to the Sx,
        Sy, and Sz operators of the readout spin.
    n_jobs : int, optional
        Number of parallel workers used to evaluate the delay times. ``-1`` uses all
        available CPU cores, while ``1`` runs the calculation serially.

    Returns
    -------
    tau_array : np.ndarray
        Array of delay times (in ns) used for the calculation.
    results : np.ndarray
        Two-dimensional array of final expectation values with shape
        ``(len(tau_array), len(e_ops))``.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If any value in ``tau_array`` is negative.

    Notes
    -----
    The first pi/2 pulse is calculated once. The remainder of the sequence is then
    evaluated independently for each value in ``tau_array`` using Joblib.
    """
    tau_array = np.asarray(tau_array, dtype=float)

    if np.any(tau_array < 0):
        raise ValueError("All tau values must be non-negative.")

    if e_ops is None:
        readout = spinsys.ReadoutSpin
        e_ops = [
            Qobj(spinsys.Sx[readout]),
            Qobj(spinsys.Sy[readout]),
            Qobj(spinsys.Sz[readout]),
        ]

    H_free = RotFrameSecular(spinsys, spinsys.f_RF)

    Omega_R = 2.0 * np.pi * spinsys.RabiRate
    tp_90 = np.pi / (2.0 * Omega_R)
    tp_180 = np.pi / Omega_R

    pulse_op = Qobj(spinsys.Sx_rot)
    H_pulse = H_free + Omega_R * pulse_op

    psi0 = spinsys.psi0
    c_ops = spinsys.collapse_ops

    # Only retain the final state from each segment.
    options = {
        "store_states": False,
        "store_final_state": True,
        "progress_bar": "",
        "method": "diag",
    }

    def evolve_final(H, state, duration):
        duration = float(duration)

        if duration == 0.0:
            return state

        result = mesolve(
            H,
            state,
            [0.0, duration],
            c_ops=c_ops,
            e_ops=None,
            options=options,
        )
        return result.final_state

    # This segment is identical for every tau, so calculate it once.
    state_after_first_90 = evolve_final(H_pulse, psi0, tp_90)

    def calc_point(tau):
        state = state_after_first_90

        # Free evolution for tau.
        state = evolve_final(H_free, state, tau)

        # Pi pulse.
        state = evolve_final(H_pulse, state, tp_180)

        # Second free evolution.
        state = evolve_final(H_free, state, tau)

        return np.asarray(expect(e_ops, state))

    results = Parallel(n_jobs=n_jobs)(delayed(calc_point)(tau) for tau in tau_array)

    return tau_array, np.asarray(results)

This function computes the expectation value of a single operator for every combination of microwave frequency and pulse width. The calculation requires spinsys to contain collapse_ops, RabiRate, and psi0, as well as a completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding spin operators.

Dictionary of options to pass to the QuTiP mesolve solver. If None, defaults to an empty dictionary.

None n_jobs int

Number of parallel worker processes used to evaluate the frequencies. -1 uses all available CPU cores, while 1 runs the calculation serially.

-1

Name Type Description pulsewidth_array ndarray

Array of pulse widths (in ns) used for the calculation.

frequency_array ndarray

Array of microwave frequencies (in GHz) used for the calculation.

Notes

def calc_RabiDetuningMap(
    spinsys: SpinSys,
    pulsewidth_array: np.ndarray,
    frequency_array: np.ndarray,
    e_ops: Qobj = None,
    solver_options: dict = None,
    n_jobs: int = -1,
):
    """
    Calculate a Rabi-oscillation map as a function of frequency detuning.

    This function computes the expectation value of a single operator for every
    combination of microwave frequency and pulse width. The calculation requires
    ``spinsys`` to contain ``collapse_ops``, ``RabiRate``, and ``psi0``, as well as
    a completed Hamiltonian and the corresponding spin operators.

    Parameters
    ----------
    spinsys : SpinSys
        SpinSys object containing the spin system information.
    pulsewidth_array : np.ndarray
        Array of pulse widths (in ns) for which to calculate the Rabi oscillation.
    frequency_array : np.ndarray
        Array of microwave frequencies (in GHz) for which to calculate the Rabi
        oscillation.
    e_ops : Qobj, optional
        Expectation operator to calculate. If None, defaults to the Sz operator of
        the readout spin.
    solver_options : dict, optional
        Dictionary of options to pass to the QuTiP mesolve solver. If None, defaults
        to an empty dictionary.
    n_jobs : int, optional
        Number of parallel worker processes used to evaluate the frequencies. ``-1``
        uses all available CPU cores, while ``1`` runs the calculation serially.

    Returns
    -------
    pulsewidth_array : np.ndarray
        Array of pulse widths (in ns) used for the calculation.
    frequency_array : np.ndarray
        Array of microwave frequencies (in GHz) used for the calculation.
    signal_map : np.ndarray
        Two-dimensional array of expectation values with shape
        ``(len(frequency_array), len(pulsewidth_array))``.

    Notes
    -----
    Each microwave frequency is evaluated independently. Parallel calculations use
    Joblib's ``loky`` process backend, and the returned rows retain the order of
    ``frequency_array``.
    """
    if pulsewidth_array[0] > 0:
        pulsewidth_array = np.concatenate(([0.0], pulsewidth_array))
    pulsewidth_array = np.asarray(pulsewidth_array, dtype=float)
    frequency_array = np.asarray(frequency_array, dtype=float)

    if e_ops is None:
        e_ops = Qobj(spinsys.Sz[spinsys.ReadoutSpin])

    if solver_options is None:
        solver_options = {}

    def calc_frequency(frequency):
        # Calculate the Hamiltonian in the rotating frame of the microwave field
        H_rot = RotFrameSecular(spinsys, frequency) + Qobj(
            2 * np.pi * spinsys.RabiRate * spinsys.Sx_rot
        )

        result = mesolve(
            H_rot,
            spinsys.psi0,
            pulsewidth_array,
            c_ops=spinsys.collapse_ops,
            e_ops=[e_ops],
            options=solver_options,
        )

        return np.asarray(result.expect[0])

    if n_jobs == 1 or frequency_array.size <= 1:
        signal_rows = [calc_frequency(frequency) for frequency in frequency_array]
    else:
        signal_rows = Parallel(
            n_jobs=n_jobs,
            backend="loky",
            batch_size="auto",
        )(delayed(calc_frequency)(frequency) for frequency in frequency_array)

    if signal_rows:
        signal_map = np.asarray(signal_rows)
    else:
        dtype = float if e_ops.isherm else complex
        signal_map = np.empty((0, pulsewidth_array.size), dtype=dtype)

    return pulsewidth_array, frequency_array, signal_map

    ``RabiRate``, and ``psi0``, as well as a completed Hamiltonian and the
    corresponding spin operators.

        e_ops=e_ops,
        options=solver_options,
    )

    return pulsewidth_array, result
